obs: - [benefit] The onboarding tour could be skipped with one link ('Skip the tour, I'm completely familiar'), landing directly on Home.
- [friction] The free plan allows only 1 project, so managing multiple projects is not possible without upgrading.
- [friction] A new project is empty; tools like To-dos must be added through a plus menu before any work can start.
- [friction] Clicking the To-dos tool title opens a rename field rather than the tool, so the tool is opened via the 'Add your first to-do' link.
- [benefit] Adding a to-do is quick: one name field plus optional assignee, due date, notes and subtasks.
- [benefit] The free plan gave a ready-made empty project with a clear 'Add something to get this project started' prompt listing to-dos and documents.
- [benefit] The Add a tool menu describes each tool in one line (To-dos, Docs, Files & Images), making it easy to pick the right one for tasks versus documents.
- [friction] Tools must be added to the project one by one before use, so a new user has to learn the plus-menu to get to to-dos and docs.
- [friction] The page layout shifted after adding a tool (activity line appeared), moving the tool menu items down about 32px.
- [friction] The free plan is limited to 1 project, so a second project for a separate workstream is not possible without upgrading.
- [benefit] The project's Add a tool menu lists a Calendar tool described as 'Add events, milestones, deadlines, etc.', which maps directly onto a deadlines calendar.
- [benefit] The new Calendar's empty state offers an 'Add your first event' link, and the event form has name, dates, times, repeat, notes and people, so posting an event took three actions.
- [friction] A fresh free account has a single empty 'My Project' with no tools, so a calendar had to be added manually before any deadline could be entered.
- [friction] The posted event defaulted to today at 5:30am-6:00am, so a deadline needs its date and time changed by hand instead of being an all-day date.
